title: “Monks, what is Right Intention? Intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill-will, intention of harmlessness. Monks, this is called Right Intention.”
content: “Monks, what is Right Intention? Intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill-will, intention of harmlessness. Monks, this is called Right Intention.”

title: “Knowing this body to be like foam, Realizing its mirage-like nature, Breaking Māra’s flower-tipped arrows, One goes beyond the sight of the King of Death.”…
content:
“Knowing this body to be like foam,
Realizing its mirage-like nature,
Breaking Māra’s flower-tipped arrows,
One goes beyond the sight of the King of Death.”

“He who gathers flowers of sensual pleasures,
With mind attached, infatuated,
Death carries him away
As a flood sweeps away a sleeping village.”

“He who gathers flowers of sensual pleasures,
With mind attached, infatuated,
Before he has had his fill of sensual pleasures,
Is overpowered by death.”

title: “Whatever things, monks, are unwholesome, partaking of the unwholesome, belonging to the unwholesome side — all of them have the mind as their forerunner. The…
content: “Whatever things, monks, are unwholesome, partaking of the unwholesome, belonging to the unwholesome side — all of them have the mind as their forerunner. The mind arises first for those things, and the unwholesome states follow after.”

title: “Monks, just as a great tree, having its roots that extend downward and laterally, all those roots convey the sap upwards — that great tree,…
content: “Monks, just as a great tree, having its roots that extend downward and laterally, all those roots convey the sap upwards — that great tree, being nourished and sustained in such a way, would stand for a long time. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are clung to — craving increases. With craving as condition, clinging arises … Thus the origination of this whole mass of suffering. Monks, just as a great tree, and a man comes with a shovel and a basket. He cuts the tree’s roots … He digs a trench … he pulls out the rootlets … or he burns the tree and scatters the ashes in a strong stream of water. That great tree, with its roots cut, made like a palm stump, cannot be reborn, cannot arise again in the future. So too, monks, one who dwells seeing peril in things that are clung to — craving ceases. With the cessation of craving, clinging ceases … Thus the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: Another Elder Nun Dhīrā: Dhīrā, be steadfast, Hold fast to wholesome states. O nun, with faculties developed, Bear this last body, Having conquered the forces…
content:
Another Elder Nun Dhīrā:

Dhīrā, be steadfast,
Hold fast to wholesome states.
O nun, with faculties developed,
Bear this last body,
Having conquered the forces of Māra’s army,
Having conquered Māra with his army.

title: “Monks, when form is born, subsists, arises, and becomes manifest — that is the birth of suffering, the subsisting of disease, the manifestation of aging…
content: “Monks, when form is born, subsists, arises, and becomes manifest — that is the birth of suffering, the subsisting of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. When feeling … perception … formations … consciousness is born, subsists, arises, and becomes manifest — that is the birth of suffering, the subsisting of disease, the manifestation of aging and death. When form ceases, subsides, and passes away — that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of disease, the passing away of aging and death. When feeling … perception … formations … consciousness ceases, subsides, and passes away — that is the cessation of suffering, the subsiding of disease, the passing away of aging and death.”

title: “The mind is fickle and restless, Hard to guard, hard to restrain. The wise make it straight, Like a fletcher straightens an arrow.” “Like a…
content:
“The mind is fickle and restless,
Hard to guard, hard to restrain.
The wise make it straight,
Like a fletcher straightens an arrow.”

“Like a fish thrown on dry ground,
Wrenched from its watery home,
This mind struggles and thrashes
To escape Māra’s grip.”

“Hard to hold, fickle,
It jumps where it wishes.
Good is it to tame the mind —
A tamed mind brings happiness.”

“The mind is hard to see, subtle,
It jumps where it wishes.
The wise guard the mind —
A guarded mind brings happiness.”

title: “Short is this life — Within a hundred years one dies, And even if one lives longer, One dies of old age. People grieve for…
content:
“Short is this life —
Within a hundred years one dies,
And even if one lives longer,
One dies of old age.

People grieve for what they hold as ‘mine’ —
All possessions are impermanent.
Seeing this, one should live homeless.

What people think of as ‘mine’
Is destroyed by death.
Knowing this, the wise one
Would not incline toward ‘mine.’

As when a person wakes up,
He no longer sees what appeared in a dream,
So too, a beloved person who dies
Is no longer seen.

Those who are seen and heard
Are called by such and such a name —
Only the name remains
For one who has passed away.

People who are greedy for ‘mine’
Do not abandon sorrow, lamentation,
And stinginess.
Therefore, sages, leaving behind attachments,
Live seeing safety.”

title: “Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained…
content: “Monks, these six sense bases — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness. What six? The eye sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. The ear … The nose … The tongue … The body … The mind sense base, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — brings happiness. These six sense bases, monks — well-guarded, well-protected, well-guarded, well-restrained — bring happiness.”

title: Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa recited this verse to the Venerable Ānanda: Sensual desire burns me, My mind is on fire. It is good, O disciple…
content:
Then the Venerable Vaṅgīsa recited this verse to the Venerable Ānanda:
Sensual desire burns me,
My mind is on fire.
It is good, O disciple of Gotama,
Out of compassion,
Teach me the Dhamma to extinguish the blaze.

(Ānanda):
It is because of distorted perception
That your mind is on fire.
Abandon the sign of the beautiful
That is connected with sensual desire.
See formations as impermanent,
Suffering, and not-self —
Extinguish great sensual desire,
Do not be burned again and again.
Develop the mind on foulness,
Unified, well-concentrated,
Practice mindfulness of the body,
Develop much disenchantment.
Practice the signless,
Destroy the underlying tendency to conceit,
And by thoroughly penetrating conceit,
Your practice will be at peace.
